| The Still Water | The far end of the lake, where nobody fishes. |

**Getting to Ashvale.** A day's walk north.

**What people say**

- Nobody fishes the Still Water. Nobody says why.
- Wren can talk anyone into anything.
- The lake is deeper than it should be.

entities.name: Tobias Vale
entities.summary:
*The Pact's spymaster, and the first of the Vales to leave home.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Human | Mystic | He/him | Ashen Spire, the Hollow Marches |

**Looks.** A neat man in his late thirties, prematurely grey, in clothes so ordinary they are almost a disguise.

**Manner.** Courteous and dry. Already knows how this conversation ends.

**Who they are**

- Spymaster of the Shadow Pact, in [The Eternal Veil](/player/e/REG-005).
- Of the Vale family, a minor house of Ashen Spire, and the first of the Vales to leave. Brother to [Brother Altharion Vale](/player/e/NPC-020), [Professor Orin Vale](/player/e/NPC-007) and [Sister Elyra Vale](/player/e/NPC-006).

**What people say**

- Tobias Vale wins every fight before it starts.
- He keeps a file on his own family.

entities.name: Tormek Ironheart
entities.summary:
*A dwarven juggernaut in armour he built himself. No blade has pierced it.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dwarf | Artificer | He/him | The Anvil of Dominion, the Tyrant's Dominion |

**Looks.** A stout dwarf almost never seen out of his own armour: black iron plates, riveted and glowing faintly at the seams.

**Manner.** Gruff, practical and endlessly tinkering. Answers questions about his armour in exhausting detail.

**Who they are**

- A dwarven juggernaut of the Crimson Legion, in [The Tyrant's Dominion](/player/e/REG-003).
- Built his own armour at the Anvil of Dominion.

**What people say**

- No blade has ever pierced his defence.
- He sleeps in the armour.
- He is building a second suit, and nobody knows who it is for.

entities.name: Torren Kell
entities.summary:
*A scavenger captain who wants wealth without allegiance, and avoids the Scar.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Earth Genasi | Rogue | He/him | The Scar, the Hollow Marches |

**Looks.** A rust-coloured earth genasi whose skin is pitted like old iron, in scavenged armour from five armies.

**Manner.** Jokey and mercenary, until someone mentions the Scar.

**Who they are**

- A scavenger captain in [The Hollow Marches](/player/e/REG-001).
- Wants wealth without allegiance.

**What people say**

- His crew will not go near the Scar.
- Ask him why and he changes the subject.

entities.name: Travel between continents
entities.summary:
*Two weeks by sea in the dark, or through the Rift, if you dare.*

**By sea.** Ships cross the Black Tides between Kaelholm and the ports of the Eternal Veil in about two weeks. Crews douse every lantern over the trench where the Rift runs beneath the sunless sea. Regular crossings have only recently begun. Smugglers also use the route.

**Through the Rift.** The Rift has one open end in the Hollow Marches and another by Ashvale. Travellers can enter one end, cross the border of the Ethereal Realm, and come out of the other. Only seasoned and very brave travellers attempt it.

entities.name: Varik "the Bloodforged"
entities.summary:
*A half-orc mercenary lord covered in contract scars. Never lost a duel.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Half-orc | Paladin | He/him | The Bleeding Arena, the Eternal Veil |

**Looks.** A broad half-orc covered in contract scars: a raised line for every oath sworn in blood.

**Manner.** Grand, honourable and theatrical. Keeps every promise to the letter.

**Who they are**

- A mercenary lord of the Bloodbound Company.

**What people say**

- Varik is covered in contract scars.
- Varik has never lost a duel.

entities.name: Varkhaal
entities.summary:
*The Crimson Legion's Iron Citadel, a city of fortresses built around the Great Arena.*

> You hear Varkhaal before you see it: a roar that rises and breaks and rises again from the Great Arena. The city is all iron and red stone, every house a little fortress, every crossroads a duelling ring. Smoke climbs out of the mountainsides around it, where the forges never stop. Soldiers of every people walk the streets in Legion red, and all of them are armed.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Tyrant's Dominion, and the seat of the Crimson Legion. Called the Iron Citadel.
- The warlords meet in the Warlord's Hall. The Legion's chief fortress, the Red Bastion, stands nearby.
- Every dispute is settled by a duel. Anyone can challenge anyone.
- The Great Arena holds a tournament every year, open to anyone. The prize is a warlord's favour.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Great Arena | The heart of the city, and its loudest place. Fights every day, and the yearly tournament. |
| The Warlord's Hall | Where the warlords meet, and where the Warlord sometimes sits. |
| The Gutter | The gladiator pits under the arena, where fighters are made, and broken. Every champion started there. |
| Karrath's Anvil | The Red Victor's shrine. Oaths are sworn with a hammer-blow on the anvil, and oath-breakers are broken on it. |
| The Bellows | Forges cut into the mountainside, smoking day and night. The Anvil of Dominion lies further down. |
| Loser Buys | A soldiers' tavern, named for its only rule. A fight a night, and no hard feelings after. |
| The Rings | A duelling circle at every crossroads. Step inside one and anyone may call you out. |
| The Red Bastion | The Legion's chief fortress, a short march from the city walls. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [Warlord Garron Kael](/player/e/NPC-024), when he is not at war, and his heir [Darion Kael](/player/e/NPC-033).
- [General Orana Volkash](/player/e/NPC-025), [Champion Valrik the Undying](/player/e/NPC-026), [Korga Bloodfang](/player/e/NPC-027) and [Velkana Stormclad](/player/e/NPC-031), usually at the arena.
- Fighters from everywhere, come for the tournament.

**Getting around**

| From Varkhaal to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hollow Refuge | About two weeks | A week to the border at the Bloodfields, a week through the iron mountains. |
| The Anvil of Dominion | Under the mountains nearby | Forge-roads, hot and crowded. |

**What people say**

- Anyone can challenge anyone in Varkhaal. Most people only do it once.
- Darion Kael holds quiet dinners with foreigners.
- The tournament draws fighters from every dominion, and some of them are spies.

Warriors are the Iron Vanguard. They fight in heavy armour and win with blocks, parries and brute force. Every army, mercenary company and caravan guard in the world is built around them.

**At the table.** A fighter, usually a Champion or a Battle Master.

entities.name: Wither's Hollow
entities.summary:
*A dead forest in endless mist, whose paths shift once you've walked past them.*

> The trees are grey and dead, and the mist never lifts. The path ahead looks clear. You walk ten steps, look back, and the path behind you is gone, and a different one is there instead. Somewhere in the mist, something is breathing.

**What you know**

- A dead, mist-bound forest in the Hollow Marches.
- Its paths shift behind travellers.
- Mother Thorn knows its trails better than anyone.

**Getting around**

| From Wither's Hollow to | Time | How safe |

| The Rift | Half a day | Openly hostile |

**What people say**

- The paths in Wither's Hollow move once you've walked past them.
- One path never moves, and nobody who follows it comes back the same.
- The forest knows who you are.

entities.name: Zepharyos
entities.summary:
*The Arcane Consortium's City of the Unbound, drifting among the clouds.*

> The city is not on the ground. It is islands of rock and tower drifting in the clouds, joined by bridges that are not always there. Some streets run sideways. One district is upside down, and the people in it seem not to mind. Lightning flickers between the spires and nobody looks up. The air tastes of metal and burnt paper.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Fractured Nexus, and the seat of the Arcane Consortium. Called the City of the Unbound.
- The council sits in the Nexus Spire. The Consortium's chief fortress, the Nexus Collegium, stands nearby.
- Magic here is limitless and unstable. Floating islands and shifting time are normal.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Nexus Spire | Where the Consortium's council sits, at the one point the whole city turns around. |
| The Nexus Collegium | The Consortium's chief fortress and greatest school. |
| The Drift | Districts on floating islands that rearrange every few nights. Maps sell out daily, and are wrong by evening. |
| The Spans | Bridges of light between the islands. Mostly reliable. |
| The Quodlibet | The great market, named for the old scholars' word for an open debate. Spell components, wands and things with no names, sold by the ounce. Some arrive before they are ordered. |
| Ithiel's Lens | The Many-Eyed's temple and observatory: knowledge, magic and the stars, watched through a thousand lenses. |
| The Antipodes | A district that flipped in some old experiment and stayed that way. Its people do not see the problem. |
| The Keel | The one inn that never moves. Nobody knows how. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [Archmagister Veylan Orithis](/player/e/NPC-034), at the Nexus Spire or the Collegium.
- [Archivist Lissara Wynne](/player/e/NPC-035), [Magister Celith Varis](/player/e/NPC-038), [Sorcerer-King Jorvas Myrr](/player/e/NPC-037), [Pyromancer Elaris Duskbane](/player/e/NPC-040) and [Master Talen Voros](/player/e/NPC-042).
- Students from every people and every dominion.

**Getting around**

| From Zepharyos to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hollow Refuge | About two weeks | A week to the border, a week through storm country. |
| The Echoing Halls and the Rift of Unmaking | Elsewhere in the Fractured Nexus | Neither is anywhere you want to be. |

**What people say**

- Half of Zepharyos floats because of something the Archmagister did by accident.
- If your island moves while you sleep, you pay rent in the new district.
- Some of the bridges lead somewhere other than the next island.
